topic: Architecture and control laws of a typical FBW system.
syllabus_extract: Architecture and control laws of a typical FBW system. Advantages and disadvantages of an FBW system.
specific_objectives: 14.2.1.1 Trainee will be able to explain the functions of AFCS.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Review of FBW block diagrams and control law definitions from IB; Instructor supervision required for diagram interpretation.
intro_questions: What is the primary function of the AFCS?
Define the term 'fly-by-wire' in the context of modern aircraft.
List three traditional mechanical control linkages used in older aircraft.

development.content:
FBW System Architecture Overview
Sensors and Signal Processing
Flight Control Computers (FCC)
Actuator Control Electronics
Control Law Logic Implementation

Gain Scheduling Principles
Stability Augmentation Systems
Protection Envelopes
Direct Law vs Normal Law
Degraded Mode Operations

Advantages of FBW Systems
Disadvantages and Risks
Redundancy Requirements
Cybersecurity Considerations
Comparison with Mechanical Systems

summary_questions: Explain how a control law modifies pilot input to ensure aircraft stability.
Identify two major advantages and two major disadvantages of implementing an FBW system.
Describe the role of the Flight Control Computer in processing sensor data.
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note comparing the pitch control interceptor logic in a typical FBW system versus a conventional mechanical system, referencing concepts introduced in LP 46.

pft_rows.syllabus: Explanation of pitch and roll control interceptors.
